Opposite Party Coram: Hon'Ble Mr.
Justice Anil Kumar Choudhary For the Petitioner : Mr. A. K. Choudhary, Adv.
 For the State : Mr. Rajneesh Vardhan, Addl. Pp

For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. R.C.P.Sah, Adv.
10 / 21.07.2023 Heard the parties.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that he does not press anticipatory bail application in respect of petitioner no. 1- Bikas Das.
Accordingly, anticipatory bail application in respect of petitioner no. 1- Bikas Das stands rejected as not pressed.

So far as the petitioner no. 2 is concerned, apprehending his arrest, the petitioner no. 2 has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Chandil P.S. Case No. 63 of 2021 registered under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner no. 2 submits that the allegation against the petitioner no. 2 is that he is the seller of the land and he approached the brother of the informant to sell property and the brother of the informant paid total consideration amount of Rs. 22,00,000/- by cash, even though the petitioner was not the owner of the said land and the petitioner is not returning the money back to the informant.
It is then submitted that the allegations against the petitioner are all false and those allegations are general and omnibus in nature.
It is further submitted that the petitioner no. 2 has taken only Rs. 50,000/- but not from the informant.
It is next submitted that the petitioner is ready to co-operate with the investigation of the case.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the dispute between the parties is at best a civil dispute and there is no material in the record to show the dishonest mis-appropriation of the Bikas Das vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

1 property by the petitioner no. 2 nor there is any allegation against the petitioner no. 2 of having any dishonest intention since the inception of the transaction between the parties.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that co-accused with similar allegations has already been granted privilege of anticipatory bail by this court vide order dated 15.02.2022 passed in ABA no. 779 of 2022, hence, the petitioner no. 2 be given the privilege of anticipatory bail on the principle of parity.

The learned Addl. PP and the learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 oppose the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner no. 2 and submits that in spite of taking money and entering into an agreement for sale, the petitioner is neither not repaying the money nor executing the sale deed,
hence, the petitioner no. 2 ought not be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to grant the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner no. 2.

Hence, in the event of arrest by the police or surrender within a period of six weeks from the date of this order, the petitioner no. 2 shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned SDJM, Seraikella in connection with Chandil P.S. Case No. 63 of 2021 subject to the condition that the petitioner no. 2 will co-operate with the Investigation of the case and will appear before the Investigating Officer as and when noticed by him and will submit mobile number and photocopy of Aadhaar card at the time of surrender in the court below with an undertaking not to change mobile number during the pendency of the case along with the other conditions laid down under section 438 (2) Cr. P.C. (ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.)
Smita/-
